about: The Nabu sha hare temple on the map page, in UTM metres (E, N) and German-zero levels like map-plan.json. Boxes are [E west, E east, N south, N north]. The plan is read off sheet C6.2 (Uppsala, CC BY 4.0) and P2021 p. 167 to 170; every height, every door and the finish are guessed and say so.

outline.src: the temple's outer faces on C6.2, its drawn wall line read at its middle: 31.9 x 34.2 m, 1,091 m2 (P2021 p. 167: about 1,080 m2); the baked-brick casing round the buried older walls lies under the street's fill at +8.0 and is not drawn

floorSrc: the rebuilt temple 'constructed on the remains of the mudbrick walls at +8.0 m' (P2021 p. 168)

paving.src: baked brick covered with asphalt, guessed as a transfer: the temple's floor 'was black with asphalt' (P2021 p. 278, on the older temple below), Pedersen's model gives this court a 'floor of bricks covered with asphalt' (P2021 p. 171, fig. 4.24), the Ishtar and Ninmah temples had black asphalt floors too (P2021 p. 279), Koldewey found an asphalt covering on the Ninmah court's pavement (K1914 ch. IX); the king's common brick about 33 cm square (P2021 p. 20); the coat's thickness and its wear ours: outside the court a thin coat, every joint full, worn thinner on the walked ways

skin.src: the court's floor as one black asphalt skin over the brick (bab.nabu.floor, guessed): young, the temple raised late in the reign, so its wear light; the skin a dull black mastic with a fine mineral grain (ours), scuffed lighter on the trodden lines (the court's door to the cella's, round the altars) and polished there by feet to a low, broad sheen where the skin shows through the film (polish: its roughness and share, ours), thin over a brick's arrises in patches so the joints ghost faintly; never bare brick, never the black bed laid open

dust.src: a thin film of dust over the asphalt (bab.wear.dust.drift, guessed): crumbled mud brick, clay-toned, thicker toward the walls' feet and in slow drifts, swept thin on the trodden lines; Koldewey saw mud brick weather to 'a light powdery dust' moved by the summer winds (K1914 ch. XLI, said of the ruins: a modern analogue); its colour a sunlit mud-brick clay, the court's earth a shade redder, its share ours, a little denser where it drifts; a film, never a heap of sand on the paved court

bounce.src: the court's floor in its walls' light under the sky field (ours): the share of the hidden sky its walls give back as the field's fit (1 + k x the walls' view factor), in the walls' colour rather than the sky's: white plaster lit by half the sky, by the sun on the share of each face the opposite wall leaves lit and by the floor's own sunlit bounce; the floor's albedo the skin under its dust film (about 0.1, ours), floorSun the floor's sunlit share as a wall's foot sees it, guessed

heights.src: ours, inside Pedersen's model's 9.0 m at most on the upper level (P2021 p. 170): the walls 6.6 m over the floor, the roof's deck 6.0, the rooms 5.4 m high, the gate towers 7.5 m and their battlements to +17.0

nabu.src: Nabu's court 14.8 x 8.7 m (P2021 p. 168), centred on its open area on C6.2

small.src: the smaller court 9.1 x 6.6 m (P2021 p. 168), on its open area on C6.2, its east side the outer wall

cella.src: Nabu's cella south of his court, 4.9 m wide, 54 m2 (P2021 p. 168): 11.0 x 4.9 m behind a 1.8 m wall

smallCella.src: the goddess's cella south of the smaller court, 3.0 m wide, 20 m2 (P2021 p. 168)

vestibule.src: guessed: a vestibule from the gate to the court, as Koldewey describes the temples' gate rooms (K1914 ch. IX, XXXIX); the gate's place on C6.2 and P2021 fig. 4.20

west1.src: guessed: a room behind a side door

west2.src: guessed: a room behind a side door

east1.src: guessed: a room behind a side door

niche.src: guessed: the cult niche in the cella's back wall (the type, P2021 p. 180), its sill 2 cm over the pedestal's top, 4.1 m over the floor at its head

doors.src: the main entrance on the street side between its towers (P2021 p. 170; C6.2, the double altar before it), plain, never arched (P2021 p. 168); width and height guessed
guessed: the vestibule's door into Nabu's court
the cella's door on the court's axis, plain (P2021 p. 168); width and height guessed
guessed, after the side doors of Pedersen's model (P2021 figs. 4.24, 4.26), plain
the goddess's cella door in the black wall, plain; width and height guessed

towers.src: the usual towers beside the main entrance (P2021 p. 170), with vertical grooves top to bottom as Koldewey found on temple fronts (K1914 ch. IX); sizes guessed (Guessed, after Koldewey, 1914, temple Z)

pilasters.src: shallow towers close together along the outer walls, each with a vertical groove top to bottom, the temples' type (K1914 ch. IX: grooves are the sacred buildings' own decoration; P2021 p. 180 on the pilasters of religious buildings); sizes guessed

merlons.src: stepped battlements, two tiers (K1914 ch. IX: the temples crowned like fortifications with the usual stepped battlements); one on each pilaster, one in each recess between, one at each corner, two over the gate, one on each fin of a gate tower; sizes guessed

bands.src: plain black bitumen bands on white lime-gypsum plaster, recorded on the older temple below (P2021 p. 167, fig. 4.23) and carried up as a transfer (Guessed); the layout after Pedersen's model of this court (P2021 fig. 4.24): a dado of black piers under two bands, black frames round the doors; no motif drawn as found; the side rooms off Nabu's court banded as the cella (P2021 p. 168: 'some other rooms nearby' had the same white walls with black bands), guessed

coat.src: the bands as a coat of bitumen paint on the plaster: it thins at its edge to a brown fringe of about a centimetre, it lies a little proud (a lit lip over each band, a shade under it), and its gloss varies with its thickness; plain bands only (SET-C1 G-C1-9)

black.src: the court wall before the goddess's cella all black with bitumen (P2021 p. 170)

ashratum.src: the Ashratum temple between the street and the Nabu temple, about 260 m2, pilasters and no towers (P2021 p. 180, 445880 E 3600400 N; C6.2): 13.4 x 19.6 m; its floor near +6 is open (P2021 p. 181); its height, finish and state at 570 BC guessed

apron.src: the open ground before the gate at the street's level (+7.5 to +8.0, P2021 p. 215), guessed, beaten earth over brick

colours.src: linear albedo, ours: lime-gypsum plaster matte and a little warm, fresh (MATERIALS, Plaster003); bitumen near black with a dull sheen (Asphalt026C), the floor's coat weathered to a dark grey-brown as old asphalt goes; the earth roof as the court's

door.opens: write in clay (feature 6): the city's name pressed into a fresh tablet on the turntable, then on paper: src/wings/babylon/clay/
door.src: the stop's one press, named by what it shows and never 'Learn more' (the words are the writer's); it stands on the court's paving at the lower right of the wide frame, clear of the grey figure and the doorways, and at the foot of the upright one, so the frame at rest keeps far more than two thirds picture

pedestal.src: the god's pedestal against the cella's back wall, its outline as drawn on C6.2 (In place: 4.7 x 2.6 m, the front corners cut, centred on the court's axis); its height ours (Guessed, 1.2 m: its face reads over the altar from the court); no statue: the statue waits for its rights row

altar.src: the court's altars before the cella's door: the block drawn on C6.2 in the court (In place as drawn: 3.4 x 2.8 m, 0.9 m off the court's south wall, centred on the axis), two low blocks drawn against the wall beside the door (In place as drawn, moved out to clear the door's guessed 2.6 m; their inner ends cut back to 0.3 m clear of the block's sides so the paving shows between, Guessed; their use not said); P2021 fig. 4.24 names them altars ('behind the altars is the door to the cella'); plastered mud brick like the double altars at the Nabu and Ninurta temples' entrances (P2021 p. 172, 175); the block as two tiers after Pedersen's model, every height and the level (on the +8.0 paving) ours (Guessed)

lamp.src: guessed: two oil lamps on stands either side of the pedestal, out of the court's sight behind the door's jambs; only their warm light is drawn

coping.src: guessed: a coping course standing 6 cm proud of each court's wall top, and on it the stepped battlements the temples were crowned with (K1914 ch. IX; the front's, ILL E05) carried round both courts; sizes and pitch ours

leaves.src: guessed: wooden leaves standing open against each door's reveal, hung at the end that opens into a room, after Pedersen's model (P2021 fig. 4.24); a sill of baked brick across each door, 5 cm over the paving, 6 cm proud of each face; the doors plain, never arched (P2021 p. 168)

wash.src: the court's walls, coping, battlements and altar blocks under the shared wash's grain (plaster-wash-babylon), as a fairly fresh coat: a white wash laid at a royal rebuilding is text-attested (CAD G pp. 53 to 54), white lime-gypsum plaster Known on the dug temples, this one included (P2021 p. 279); patches renewed between rebuilds guessed, so only faint tone patches; the mud brick under it in the baked brick's format, 33 cm in courses of about 10 cm, guessed as the throne room's; the sand of the wash only where a face is seen from afar (ours), the altar blocks seen near keep their plain plaster; no salt bloom, no damp band, no chipped edge
